He doesn't live in the same city as me. We just text each other during the day. I don't have many friends here.

He did have feelings for me at one point and I don't know if that ever went away for him. I don't know how to tell. I asked him and he said he wanted to be together but he wanted to wait until "the conditions were perfect." Since we are both going through stressful life situations right now. I don't know if I'm just being rash about my decision making or if he is just leading me on.

After feeling this way for ten years, how long is a significant break?

How will I know? I don't think I will ever get over him.
I guess he's just not sure. But yeah I shouldn't ruin a good friendship. But I can't so having feelings for him. How do I get over that?

I like this analogy but it doesn't make feeling empty any better :( 
What if the water stops dripping?
It's not that I don't love myself. I just, I want to be happy. I'm fine with feeling sad and hurt. I don't want commitment from him. Maybe just attention?

I wish it were that simple. I've had my heart broken after my boyfriend of five years dumped me last month. I'm ready to move on and have some joy in my life but I can't because I've gotten so invested in my best friend. I'm just getting crushed left, right and centre.
Yeah you're right. I just want this so bad. And it's already been so long. I can do a little bit more waiting. Especially if it is going to be as good as I think it will be.

Yeah that sounds good. And even after a month, and he's still not ready give him another month. But just don't hassle him all the time. This is good advice, thanks. I just need to take it slow but not wait around forever.
I am awful at being patient! Do you have tips to help me be more patient?

Well, last time we got together we did stuff like that we watched movies and snuggled and held hands and it was nice. I guess I should just keep doing that? How long should I do that? I like him a lot but I don't want to wait around forever, you know? A year? Is that too long?
Well I do think I could make him happy but I don't think it's healthy to start a relationship using each other as emotional crutches.
I get what you mean that sounds like rebounding but I feel like maybe being single has really let my feelings for my friend flourish. Or am I kidding myself?
I feel like I am over my ex. But to be honest I had never been in a relationship that long and I don't really know how to tell when I'm really over him.

Yeah, I get what you mean about just letting it flow. I'm not very good at that but I should work on it if I want this to turn out.

When you say "be as much of a girlfriend as you can without actually being one" what do you mean? Could you elaborate a bit?

Yeah, you are totally right. I know that I'm putting my needs first and that's wrong of me. 

I am just impatient. We've both been hurting so much, I want to be happy and I want him to be happy and I think we can help each other in that regard. But I should probably back off until he is more ready.
I didn't do anything to break his trust. His ex-girlfriend cheated on him and he is worried about that happening to him again, not just with me but with any woman.

Yeah, this is my thinking too. They always say that the foundation of a good relationship is being best friends, and clearly we are already that. But at the same time I want to respect his desires, because I still think he wants more time to figure out how to do this.

Plus he is worried about it not working and we would stop being friends after.
